Eighteen UFC fights at full trust means none of that is shrunk or speculative — it is the most thoroughly measured decline on the card.

The KO threat differential says the rest: +1.86 for Pinto against −0.07 for Spann, the largest such gap of the night. Pinto's 83.7% is 56.0% KO, 3.7% submission and 24.0% decision; Spann's 16.3% is interesting in that his best single route is a 7.0% submission rather than a 4.9% knockout — consistent with a career 45.5% submission finish rate and first-round submissions of Brzeski and Saint Preux. This is also the only fight on the card the model expects to end inside the first round more often than not: Over 1.5 is just 47.9% and Over 2.5 only 32.6%, with 21,227 of 50,000 sims finishing in round one.

synopsis.body: The card's clearest projection and its most violent: Pinto 83.7% with a 60.9% total KO rate. Undefeated at 12-0 with 100% takedown defence, 65.7% head accuracy and no negative composite, against a Spann whose chin (−1.42) is the worst value on the card and whose damage factor has hit the model's 0.500 floor after being finished in 85.7% of his losses. KO threat differential +1.86 to −0.07. Spann's live route is a submission (7.0%), not a knockout (4.9%). The only fight here more likely than not to end in round one — Over 1.5 just 47.9%.

composites.note: Positive = above weight-class avg. ±0.5 = clear edge, ±1.0 = elite/poor.

Recent: W vs Christian Edwards (Decision R3, 2026-05-16) | L vs Nikita Krylov (KO/TKO R3, 2026-01-24) | W vs Paul Craig (KO/TKO R1, 2025-09-06)

matchupAnalysis: The card's second Elo disagreement, and a starker one than Keita's: Sy is favoured at 77.8% while sitting 111 points BELOW Bukauskas on the ratings (1575 over five divisional fights against 1686 over twelve). Unlike the Keita fight, though, the two engines here are in near-total agreement — GBM 77.1%, hand-tuned 77.6% — so the disagreement is specifically between the outcome-based rating and everything else, not an unresolved argument inside the model. Elo is reading Sy's recent 1-2 stretch; the composites are reading the physical and durability mismatch underneath it.

That mismatch is large. Sy's reach composite is +2.97 — the single highest value of any fighter on this card (210.82 cm against Bukauskas's 193.04, a seven-inch gap), alongside chin +0.80 and output +0.77 on 0.98 head strikes absorbed per minute and a +1.54 strike differential. Bukauskas is the more experienced and more fully-trusted fighter (13 fights, trust 1.000) but the trusted picture is a bleak one: chin −1.15, a chin damage factor of 0.524 just off the model's floor, finished in 80% of his losses, early vulnerability +0.66, and a third-round KO loss to Nikita Krylov in January. The KO threat spread is the widest structural gap of the night: Sy +1.21 against Bukauskas −1.75.

Two things cut against the projection and belong in the record. First, Sy is 1-2 in his last three and lost his most recent fight by first-round submission to Ion Cutelaba in March — and Bukauskas beat that same Cutelaba by decision, a common opponent whose result points the wrong way for the favourite. Second, Sy is on trust 0.612 from five fights while Bukauskas is fully observed, so the profile driving this is the less certain of the two. The method split reads 35.0% Sy KO against a 46.7% total decision rate, and the O/U engines agree unusually tightly here (sim 49.4%, GBM 49.4% on Over 2.5) — a coin-flip on the distance at Over 2.5 49.7%.

synopsis.body: Sy 77.8% despite an 111-point Elo deficit — but with both engines within 0.5pp of each other, so the model is united and only the rating dissents. It is built on the card's largest physical edge (reach +2.97, seven inches) meeting the card's second-worst durability profile: Bukauskas at chin −1.15, damage factor 0.524, finished in 80% of his losses. KO threat +1.21 against −1.75. Against it: Sy is 1-2 in his last three, was submitted in round one by Cutelaba, and Bukauskas beat that same Cutelaba — a common opponent pointing the wrong way. Distance is a coin-flip (Over 2.5 at 49.7%).
